title: User Context
explain: User context is the bundle of known facts about a user at request time, evaluated with exact rules like `country in [US, CA] AND plan == "pro" AND app_version >= 4.2`. Use it when a decision must be precise, deterministic and explainable: feature flags, entitlements, pricing, experiments. An embedding says 'probably similar'; a rule says 'true or false'. (用户的多个特征, 做精确 rule matching.)
model:
**What goes in the context:** identity and account (plan, tenant, role), environment (country, locale, device, app version), recent behaviour (segments, last seen).

```
request ─▶ authenticate ─▶ load attributes ─▶ immutable context snapshot
        ─▶ evaluate rules in priority order ─▶ decision
        ─▶ log (rule id, context version)
```

**Design rules**
- **One immutable snapshot per request**; every rule sees the same facts.
- **Define missing values.** Unknown is not false. State per rule type: for grants, fail closed (no match); for deny rules, the safe default may be the opposite.
- **Precedence:** first-match-wins over an ordered list, or all-matching. Order is part of the policy.
- **Freshness:** attributes have a TTL; know which may be stale (a just-upgraded plan).
- **Stable bucketing** for experiments: hash a stable id ([hash bucketing](#/sd/f/hash-bucketing)).
- **Privacy:** pass only what a rule needs; do not log raw PII.

Contrast with an [item embedding](#/sd/f/item-embedding).

details.q: Rules or embeddings for 'restrict this feature to approved countries'?
details.a: Rules. It is a compliance-style yes/no that must be exact and auditable. A similarity or clustering approach can be wrong for an individual user, and a Bloom filter admits false positives. Use embeddings only for fuzzy relevance such as recommendations.

details.q: Why one immutable snapshot per request?
details.a: So all rules and all services in the request evaluate the same facts. If attributes were re-read per rule, a plan change mid-request could make two rules disagree, and you could not reproduce the decision afterwards from the logged context version.

details.q: A rule grants a discount when `signup_source != "affiliate"` and the attribute is missing because the profile service timed out. What now?
details.a: Treat the comparison as unknown, so the rule does not match and no discount is granted; record the missing attribute. A missing value is not a value that differs from 'affiliate'. Conventions differ for deny rules, so state them per rule type.

details.q: How do first-match-wins rules work in practice?
details.a: Rules are evaluated in order and the first match decides. With (1) plan == enterprise, (2) country in [DE, FR] AND device == mobile, (3) country == DE, a free-plan mobile user in DE is decided by rule 2; rule 3 also matches but is never reached. Changing the order changes the policy, so review order like code.

details.q: Why not precompute decisions for every combination of attributes?
details.a: It explodes exponentially: 5 attributes with 4 values each is 4^5 = 1,024 combinations, and real attributes have many more values. Evaluate the rules against the one user's context at request time instead.

details.q: How do you keep rule decisions explainable and debuggable?
details.a: Log the decision with the matching rule id, the context version and any missing attributes, so you can replay it later. Version the rule set too, and support a dry-run mode that evaluates a new rule against recent traffic before enabling it.

Assign users to buckets by hashing a stable id with the experiment name, so assignment is deterministic and sticky, then let rules refer to the bucket as one more attribute. Do not assign randomly per request.

prompts.q: Explain user context and when you would use it instead of an embedding.
points: Known attributes at request time matched by exact rules
Embedding gives fuzzy similarity, not a guarantee

prompts.q: Walk through how a rule engine handles one request.
points: Authenticate, then load attributes into an immutable snapshot
Evaluate rules in priority order, first match wins
Log rule id and context version
Ordering is part of the policy

prompts.q: What do you define for missing and stale attributes?
points: Fail closed for grants, per-rule-type convention for denies
TTLs on cached attributes, know which can be stale
Privacy: minimal attributes, no raw PII in logs
